title: Hierarchy-matched Llama7B router post-route activity power
hypothesis: Applying the exact cycle-verified node-5 Llama7B replay to the matching routed bare-router hierarchy will replace vectorless/scaled intrinsic-router energy without attributing synthetic harness, link, or memory power to the router.

direct_comparison.primary_question: What intrinsic routed energy does one interior router consume for the complete checked Llama7B Phase 2 replay?
include: all timing-feasible uniquely routed bare-router utilization points
direct VCD and sequential-register activity annotation
separate annotation-clock dynamic energy and physically feasible leakage duration
exclude: synthetic PPA traffic and observation harness
inter-router links and aggregate mesh clock tree

expected_benefit: replace intrinsic router vectorless power with workload activity
preserve energy/area/timing sensitivity across physical utilization points
provide an exact hierarchy anchor for the next Llama7B transport recost
risks: one interior router does not measure spatial activity variation or aggregate link power
the checked schedule uses a 1 ns source clock; the identical cycle sequence must be explicitly retimestamped to the routed target clock while retaining both clocks in provenance
raw VCD, ODB, and SPEF stay evaluator-local

required_evaluations.objective: Measure hierarchy-matched routed node-5 router activity power for the complete Llama7B Phase 2 replay.

expected_result.reason: The result must retain every physical point and choose energy only among timing-feasible routes with complete activity gates.
